title: Advancing Education through Tutoring Systems: A Systematic Literature Review
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the broad question of how tutoring systems have evolved and what benefits, limitations, and ethical concerns characterize modern AI-enabled tutoring. The authors review the literature on Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) and Robot Tutoring Systems (RTS), with special attention to adaptive learning, engagement, scalability, and responsible AI use. Their goal is to synthesize five decades of work, from early computer-assisted instruction to current systems using Bayesian Knowledge Tracing and large language models such as ChatGPT.

The intervention/approach studied is not a single implementation but a systematic literature review following PRISMA. The authors screened 340 records and included 86 representative studies published from 1972 to 2024. They analyzed studies across dimensions of artificial intelligence, system behavior, engagement, affordances, and ethics, and also performed latent class analysis to group tutoring systems into computer-based ITS, robot-based verbal tutoring systems, and multimodal systems.

The review does not focus on one population or site, but it does note examples in elementary, middle school, secondary, and higher education contexts. A recurring example is middle school mathematics tutoring, and the paper also references robot-child tutoring and LLM-based tutoring in physics and language learning. The main conclusion is that software-based ITS generally offer stronger cognitive adaptability and scalability, while robot-based systems better support social and emotional engagement. The authors argue that hybrid systems combining both strengths may be most promising, but that ethical issues such as privacy, transparency, bias, and the risk of hallucinations remain important unresolved challenges.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic literature review following PRISMA, so it has a clear methodology and broad synthesis value. However, it is not a meta-analysis or a primary experimental study, and the paper does not report pooled effect sizes or causal estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The review suggests meaningful benefits for learning, engagement, and scalability, but the evidence is synthesized qualitatively and no pooled effects are reported. The overall impact is therefore promising but still unclear in magnitude for K-12 practice.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of computer-based intelligent tutoring systems using adaptive algorithms such as Bayesian Knowledge Tracing and large language models to deliver personalized instruction, feedback, and real-time difficulty adjustment across educational contexts, including mathematics.

Systematic review of robot tutoring systems that use physical, semi-anthropomorphic, and fully anthropomorphic robots to provide verbal feedback, gestures, social presence, and embodied interaction for tutoring and engagement.
Review of generative AI and chatbot-enabled tutoring within tutoring systems, including ChatGPT-like models used for adaptive tutoring, natural language feedback, and conversational learning support.

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature (86 studies), tutoring systems were reported to improve learning outcomes through personalized and adaptive instruction, with modern systems using BKT and LLMs to tailor content and feedback in real time. The paper does not provide a pooled effect size, but it repeatedly characterizes learning gains as significant and comparable in some cases to one-on-one tutoring; no single study-level estimate is synthesized in the review text.
finding.measure: Learning outcomes / academic achievement reported across included tutoring-system studies

finding.finding_summary: The review finds that robot-based and multimodal tutoring systems improve engagement, motivation, and social-emotional connection through verbal encouragement, gestures, eye contact, and human-like presence. These effects are described qualitatively across the included studies rather than pooled into a meta-analytic estimate.
finding.measure: Engagement, motivation, and social-emotional response indicators reported in included studies

finding.finding_summary: The review argues that software-based tutoring systems are relatively easy to deploy and scale because they rely on existing computer infrastructure and cloud-based delivery, whereas robot-based systems are more costly and complex. This is a conceptual synthesis rather than an effectiveness estimate, so no effect size is reported.

The paper identifies important ethical and governance challenges—especially data privacy, transparency, algorithmic bias, and access inequities—while also describing mitigation strategies such as encryption, audits, access controls, and oversight committees. These institutional impacts are discussed as emerging risks and best-practice recommendations rather than measured outcomes.
finding.measure: Ethical concerns, governance practices, and responsible-AI safeguards in tutoring systems
